column1: Day 1: Mix 50g whole wheat or whole rye flour with 50g room-temperature drinking water in a clean jar, leaving plenty of room for expansion. Scrape down the sides, mark the starting level with a rubber band, and cover loosely or use a vented lid; do not seal airtight. Keep at about 24–26°C (75–79°F), out of direct sunlight.

Day 2, about 24 hours later: Keep 50g of the mixture and discard the rest. Stir in 50g bread flour and 50g water. Mark the level and cover loosely. Use a clean jar if the sides are crusted. Bubbles or an early rise are normal, but do not mean the starter is ready.

Day 3: Repeat the feeding after about 24 hours: retain 50g starter, discard the rest, and add 50g bread flour and 50g water. Mark the level and cover loosely. Activity may slow after the first burst; keep feeding even if there is little visible rise.

Day 4: Continue the same feeding, retaining 50g starter and adding 50g bread flour and 50g water. Check the marked level. If it rises to a peak and starts falling well before the next daily feeding, switch to feeding about every 12 hours.

Day 5: Keep feeding every 24 hours, or every 12 hours if it is peaking and falling sooner. At each feeding, retain 50g starter, discard the rest, and add 50g bread flour and 50g water. Look for increasing bubbles, a pleasantly tangy or yeasty smell, and a more predictable rise.
Day 6: Repeat the same feeding schedule and amounts. Track how long it takes to double after feeding. Do not bake with it yet if it only bubbles without rising reliably.

Day 7 and beyond: The starter is ready when it reliably doubles within about 4–8 hours of feeding at 24–26°C (75–79°F) for at least 2–3 consecutive feedings, with plenty of bubbles and a pleasantly tangy smell. If it is not ready, continue the same feedings; a new starter may need two weeks or longer.

Throughout the process: Do not taste the raw mixture or use the early discard in food. If you see fuzzy mold or pink or orange discoloration, discard the entire starter, clean the equipment thoroughly, and start again.
